title: [Windows] HDR AdvancedColorInfoChanged callback accesses windows[] without guard and queue shutdown does not await in-flight callbacks
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: `master` @ `a8643700ce` (4.7-dev); not yet present in 4.6.x stable (the `AdvancedColorInfoChanged` path was added in #118339, merged 2026-04-09 and landed on master 2026-04-16).

### System information

Windows 11 24H2, any editor build where the `WINRT_ENABLED` path is compiled. Reproducible on both dedicated-GPU HDR displays and on WSL’d display stacks that report HDR capability via WinRT.

### Issue description

Two correctness problems were introduced on master alongside the new WinRT `AdvancedColorInfo` listener in #118339:

1. `DisplayServerWindows::_winrt_adv_color_info_cb` and `DisplayServerWindows::_get_screen_hdr_data` access `windows[p_window]` without the `ERR_FAIL_COND(!windows.has(...))` guard that every other public method on that class uses. The WinRT event is dispatched through `call_deferred`, so the window ID can already be gone by the time the deferred call executes. `HashMap::operator[]` on a missing key either auto-inserts a default `WindowData` (non-const) or is UB (const); neither is intended.

2. `WinRTUtils::destroy_queue` calls `controller.ShutdownQueueAsync()` without awaiting the returned `IAsyncAction`. During `~DisplayServerWindows`, an in-flight `AdvancedColorInfoChanged` callback can run against partially-destroyed members.

Code references:

- `platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp:3410-3412` and `:3458-3459`
- `platform/windows/winrt_utils.cpp:134-136`

### Steps to reproduce

Crash path (requires an HDR-capable monitor):

1. Launch an editor build with `WINRT_ENABLED` on a Windows 11 machine with at least one HDR-capable secondary monitor.
2. Open a second editor window on that monitor and drag it around.
3. In Windows Settings → System → Display, toggle "Use HDR" on and off repeatedly, at roughly 1 Hz. Each toggle fires `AdvancedColorInfoChanged` and schedules a deferred `_winrt_adv_color_info_cb` on the main loop.
4. Close the second window at the moment of a toggle.
5. Observed: the deferred callback executes with a stale `WindowID` — `windows[p_id]` auto-inserts a fresh default `WindowData` entry (memory leak) in debug, or hits UB/crash in release depending on compiler codegen of the const `operator[]` in `_get_screen_hdr_data`.

Shutdown race (deterministic on a debug build):

1. Put a breakpoint at the `controller.ShutdownQueueAsync()` call in `WinRTUtils::destroy_queue`.
2. Repeatedly exit the editor while an HDR toggle is in-flight on any secondary monitor.
3. Observe a callback executing after destructor-side member teardown has begun.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A — this is a platform-level bug reachable through standard editor use on Windows 11 with an HDR-capable secondary display. Any empty Godot 4.7-dev project triggers it under the same toggle-during-close sequence.

### Proposed fix

Open as #118669 — adds `ERR_FAIL_COND(!windows.has(...))` / `ERR_FAIL_COND_V(...)` to the two HDR entry points, and switches `destroy_queue` to `controller.ShutdownQueueAsync().get()` so teardown drains in-flight events.
